Forecasting Electrical Load and Renewable Energy Generation Using Machine Learning Methods
nodes.venue: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
nodes.abstract: This chapter per the authors examines machine learning for forecasting electrical load and renewable generation under energy transition and grid digitalization. The purpose is to show why power systems need models handling nonlinear, non-stationary, and heterogeneous data. The chapter reviews LSTM, BiLSTM, GRU, CNN, TCN, hybrid architectures, ensembles, SVR, and GPR. Solar and wind forecasting depend on weather uncertainty, spatial relationships, and telemetry quality. The chapter compares facility types with forecasting methods and discusses digital twins, adaptive forecasting, and closed-loop control. Key problems: data drift, limited transferability, interpretability, computational complexity, and SCADA cybersecurity. Development requires integrating forecasting with digital twins, XAI, reinforcement learning, anomaly detection, and cybersecurity. Machine learning becomes a foundation for proactive and resilient power system management.

nodes.name: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
Advancing Sign Language for Neurodivergent Learners in Inclusive Secondary Schools
nodes.venue: Designing and Implementing Literacy Ecosystems
nodes.abstract: This chapter advances Zambian Sign Language literacy as a practical, affordable and effective strategy for promoting educational access and participation among neurodivergent learners in inclusive Zambian secondary schools. It is based on neurodiversity-affirming principles in discussing neurological differences (autism spectrum disorder, dyslexia, dyspraxia) as natural variations in human cognition rather than deficits to be fixed. The chapter demonstrates how ZSL's visual-spatial and multimodal nature link with neurodivergent cognitive strengths by reducing cognitive load, improving expressive and receptive communication, supporting emotional regulation and promoting social inclusion. It proposes lifelike low-cost strategies through Universal Design for Learning, teacher professional development, family, community engagement and targeted policy reform. The chapter contends that widespread adoption of ZSL literacy can transform inclusive education in Zambia and promote sustainable development goals, 3 (Good Health and Well-Being); 4 (Quality Education); 10 (Reduced Inequalities).

nodes.name: Wetbird-DETR: Detection of Waterbirds in Satellite Wetlands of the Middle and Lower Reaches of the Yangtze River, China
nodes.venue: Waterbirds
nodes.abstract: The wetlands of the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River provide important habitats for migratory waterbirds, but repeated image-based monitoring in small satellite wetlands is difficult because birds are often distant, partly hidden by vegetation, and photographed against complex backgrounds. Here, the use of automated object detection was evaluated as a support tool for waterbird monitoring in these habitats. A lightweight detector, WetBird-DETR, was developed for field images collected in satellite wetlands. The detector was evaluated with a regional dataset from six satellite wetland sites in Anhui and Jiangsu Provinces, China, collected from June 2024 to June 2025 and containing 10 common waterbird species under varied light and background conditions. Supplementary evaluations were also conducted using two public bird datasets. WetBird-DETR maintained competitive detection performance while reducing the number of parameters and computational cost relative to the baseline detector. The results indicate that automated detection can support preliminary image screening, initial localization of birds, and expert review in repeated surveys of satellite wetlands. Broader validation across regions, seasons, habitat types, waterbird communities, and imaging systems will be necessary before the model can be used to support wider ecological inference.

nodes.name: Validating a Novel Above-Ground Corrosion Assessment Methodology for Unpiggable Pipelines
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract A significant portion of the world's buried pipeline infrastructure remains inaccessible to In-line Inspection (ILI), necessitating alternative integrity assessment methods. This paper presents the test validation of Current Magnetometry Inspection (CMI), a non-intrusive above-ground technique for detecting coating-related defects and classifying external corrosion activity on buried pipelines, including midstream export, transmission, and distribution pipelines, as well as upstream production flowlines and gathering systems. This combination of coating defect detection and corrosion activity characterization provides information not available through conventional above-ground inspection methods. The technique measures the magnetic field generated in a pipeline by a multi-frequency alternating current (AC) source, making it an active magnetometry technique distinct from passive magnetometry. External corrosion defects associated with coating damage produce perturbations in the measured magnetic field response. A controlled blind validation test was conducted in partnership with a major pipeline operator using a fabricated test pipe spool. Defects representing actively corroding sites, passivated corrosion, and a simulated repair were introduced at undisclosed locations. Surveys were performed without prior knowledge of defect locations, dimensions, or corrosion states, and results were compared against the documented ground truth for the fabricated defects. The validation demonstrated successful detection of all blind corrosion-related defects introduced in the test specimen, with the simulated repair defect correctly not reported as a corrosion indication. Closely spaced defects below the specified spatial resolution were reported as combined defects, while detected defect locations remained within typical excavation assessment lengths. Corrosion activity characterization was demonstrated, with all medium- and high-confidence classifications correctly identified, while misclassifications occurred only among low-confidence results. While this demonstrates that data confidence assessment provides a consistent indicator for interpreting corrosion activity classification results, a low-confidence passivated classification should be conservatively considered potentially active to reduce the risk of overlooking actively corroding locations. Beyond validating CMI performance, the study also identifies recommendations for improving the technical rigor of future qualification programs for emerging inspection technologies. As an above-ground inspection alternative, CMI addresses integrity management challenges for buried pipeline assets beyond the reach of conventional ILI. Conventional potential-based inspection methods such as Direct Current Voltage Gradient (DCVG), Alternating Current Voltage Gradient (ACVG), and Close Interval Potential Survey (CIPS) can identify coating holidays but cannot determine local corrosion activity, potentially resulting in unnecessary excavations or missed active corrosion sites. By combining coating-related defect detection with corrosion activity characterization, CMI provides integrity information beyond conventional potential-based inspection methods and supports more informed integrity decision-making for buried pipeline applications.

nodes.name: Topology-Aware Graph Learning for Cross-Field Few-Shot Stratigraphic Correlation from Well Logs
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract Regional stratigraphic correlation becomes difficult when only a small number of target wells are interpreted and the well pattern is spatially uneven. This study proposes a topology-aware graph framework for cross-field few-shot stratigraphic correlation from well logs. A sequence encoder was pretrained on 87 interpreted wells from a mature source field using gamma ray, acoustic transit time, and resistivity logs. Because the source and target fields use different stratigraphic label systems, the source-specific prediction head was discarded and only the pretrained encoder was transferred; a target-specific head was then adapted using six labeled wells from a 37- well target dataset. Target wells were selected using predictive uncertainty, spatial coverage, and feature redundancy. Regional correlation was then performed on a spatial-relational graph constrained by stratigraphic order, while expert corrections were introduced as fixed anchors for controlled refinement. The framework reduced mean horizon-depth error from 2.85 m to 1.84 m, and expert-anchor refinement further reduced it to 1.51 m, an 18.0% improvement. The results show that cross-field representation transfer and topology- aware regional reasoning can reduce target-field interpretation requirements without assuming direct correspondence between source and target stratigraphic labels.

nodes.name: Thickness sensing and anomaly detection for shotcrete support in roadways based on machine learning
nodes.venue: Measurement Science and Technology
nodes.abstract: Abstract Abstract: Aiming at the problem that the shotcrete thickness detection in roadway engineering relies on discrete manual spot checks and it is difficult to identify continuous low-thickness regions, this paper constructs the Full-field Thickness Perception and Anomaly Detection Method (FTP-AD). Taking the two-phase LiDAR point clouds before and after shotcreting as input, this method establishes the surface correspondence through global registration and ROI local registration, and uses floor correction and principal normal translation preservation to reduce the offset of registration to the change of shotcrete thickness. Subsequently, while retaining the candidate points at high-curvature boundaries, sparse outliers are eliminated, a finite-length normal cylindrical neighborhood is used to estimate the local thickness, and the thickness field is formed through median smoothing, then the connected low-thickness regions are extracted combined with the designed thickness limit. Verified by 20 measuring points on a single roadway interface, the results show that the mean absolute error of FTP-AD is 4.52 mm and the root mean square error is 5.69 mm, both lower than the comparison configurations using traditional ICP, point-to-plane ICP and M3C2. The ablation results further indicate that both floor correction and principal normal translation preservation help to reduce the thickness measurement error. In this case, the proposed method realizes the spatial expression of the shotcrete thickness distribution and the concentrated low-thickness positions, and provides quantitative information for the quality evaluation of roadway shotcrete support.

nodes.name: The Skills Intelligence Engine for an AI-Ready Energy Workforce
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract As digitalization and AI reshape the energy industry, operators must transform large technical workforces without eroding core domain expertise. The challenge goes beyond training digital specialists; it requires evolving domain professionals into domain-plus-AI, domain-plus-digital, and domain-plus-business practitioners. This paper presents a framework of energy organization's Skills Intelligence Infrastructure, a single engine linking learning activity, curated curricula, skills maps, HR data, and a conversational AI agent (beta) that bridges HR and business to support upskilling, mobility, promotion readiness, and strategic workforce planning. The infrastructure was developed through a four-layer architecture. First, a unified data foundation integrates employee learning activity with HR data, enabling segmentation by role, organization, geography, seniority, and business area. Second, curated curricula and skills maps are designed with business owners to align with enterprise priorities across AI, machine learning, data, operations, sustainability, project management, safety-critical training, sales, and domain competence. These resources support aspirational and promotion-linked roles while clarifying expectations, gaps, and priorities. Third, persona-driven experiences serve employees and managers: employees pursue pathways, identify gaps and future requirements, and build T-shaped capability—deep domain expertise broadened by AI, digital, project, and business skills—while managers monitor development, assess the regional distribution of skills, and identify talent opportunities for mobility, promotion, and hiring. Fourth, a conversational AI agent lets employees ask which skills target roles require and which pathways to prioritize, while managers evaluate talent against skills, learning records, pathway completion, and readiness indicators. Deployed across approximately 8,000 professionals, the platform delivers curated curricula for more than 60 aspirational roles, including 12 promotion-linked roles, and hundreds of pathways across digital, AI, data, project management, safety, sales, and domain expertise. As the enterprise system of record for capability, it provides end-to-end visibility into the AI upskilling funnel: more than 3,000 employees advancing their skills, more than 1,500 certified data science practitioners, and early identification of domain data scientist candidates. It surfaces more than 150 AI-powered innovation projects across the E&P lifecycle and tracks participation in an enterprise's strategic development program. For managers, it reveals skills trends across regions, business lines, and disciplines, exposing hidden capability gaps and talent opportunities. By favoring internal development over hiring, it has reduced recruitment costs for scarce digital talent and improved satisfaction with learning and career development. Unlike commercial talent-marketplace platforms, this skills-based workforce intelligence solution is purpose-built for a large technical energy workforce. It links HR and business through manager-owned skills maps, integrates siloed domain certifications and critical pathways, and operationalizes the domain-to-domain-plus-AI transformation at scale. It supports upskilling, talent conversion, mobility, promotion readiness, compliance tracking, and build-versus-hire decisions. Future enhancements will infer skills from roles, projects, and experience and extend the AI agent into talent management. This provides a foundation on which the energy workforce can build as AI reshapes the industry.

nodes.name: StoneXAI-Net: an explainable weakly supervised framework for kidney stone classification, localization, and segmentation from CT images
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
nodes.abstract: Introduction Kidney stone disease (urolithiasis) is one of the most frequent urological diseases worldwide; it is highly recurrent and carries a significant clinical burden and economic cost. Non-contrast computed tomography (CT) is the primary diagnostic modality and offers the highest sensitivity and specificity. However, automated kidney stone analysis remains challenging because expert pixel-level annotations are scarce, hyperdense non-stone anatomy causes mislocalization in weakly supervised localization, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods are often used circularly, both for weakly supervised localization and for its subsequent interpretation. Methods We present StoneXAI-Net, an explainable, weakly supervised framework to classify, localize, and segment kidney stones from CT images. The framework consists of three modules: (i) a CT-physics augmentation strategy that diversifies training and mitigates overfitting; (ii) consensus pseudo-labeling that combines complementary explanation maps with uncertainty maps and anatomical priors to suppress false localizations; and (iii) a faithfulness audit module with deletion, insertion, and pointing-game metrics that objectively evaluates explanation quality. The resulting consensus pseudo-labels were used to train an attention-prior-conditioned Attention U-Net for segmentation. The framework was evaluated on 3,364 axial abdominal CT images (1,577 stone and 1,787 normal) using five-fold cross-validation. Results StoneXAI-Net achieved 97.4% accuracy, 98.4% precision, 96.0% recall, a 97.1% F1-score, and a 99.5% AUC. Against consensus pseudo-masks, the full segmentation configuration achieved a proxy Dice coefficient of 0.834, an IoU of 0.777, and an HD95 of 2.94 px; anatomical post-processing reduced HD95 by 6.26 px. Discussion StoneXAI-Net is a feasible and interpretable framework for the automated analysis of kidney stones that substantially reduces the time-consuming and costly manual annotation of kidney stones by experts. Because segmentation was evaluated against pseudo-masks at the slice level, these results are proxy estimates that require confirmation with expert annotations and patient-level validation.

nodes.name: Scaling the Outcrop: An Integrated Cross-Scale Correlation Engine Bridging 3D Geological Outcrop Digital Twins with Subsurface Wellbore Analytics
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope In complex hydrocarbon exploration, particularly within ultra-deep or frontier plays, the scarcity of offset well data often leads to significant geological uncertainty during drilling deployment. Field outcrop studies supply the analogs used to close that gap, but an interpreted outcrop section is rarely registered to the same spatial and depth reference frame as the wells it informs. This paper reports the third development stage of a 3D geological outcrop digital twin platform — a cross-scale correlation engine that places an interpreted outcrop section onto a well's true-vertical-depth axis. It is deliberately positioned as a validation-framework contribution, not an applied field-validation study: it defines, freezes, and audits the geometry-level registration workflow and establishes the numerical control a later field campaign can test against. No paired outcrop-and-well field dataset is reported here. Methods, Procedures, Process The engine sits on an established foundation — UAV oblique photogrammetry, structure-from-motion reconstruction, RTK ground control, lithofacies segmentation — none of it claimed as new. Three elements are specified in full. A three-dimensional bedding-normal projection converts interpreted contacts to cumulative true stratigraphic thickness without assuming a section perpendicular to strike. A weighted multi-horizon affine model registers cumulative thickness to true vertical depth subsea, fitted on declared anchor horizons only. An auditable composite score ranks candidate outcrop-to-formation pairings on stratigraphic name, lithology, relative position, and marker-bed evidence. Lacking a paired field dataset, numerical behavior was examined through a disclosed synthetic benchmark: a nested ablation over 1,000 Monte Carlo realizations with ten held-out horizons, and a 4,000-trial semantic-mapping stress test with an 80-variant weight-sensitivity grid. Every parameter, equation, weight, and random seed is reported. Results, Observations, Conclusions Under the declared synthetic uncertainty model, the ablation reduced mean held-out-horizon RMSE from 4.67 m for apparent thickness tied to a single datum, to 2.01 m after three-dimensional bedding-normal projection, and to 0.27 m after four-anchor affine registration, with 98.96% empirical coverage against a nominal 95% prediction interval. The deliberately ambiguous stress test raised top-1 matching accuracy from 42.45% for name similarity alone to 91.68% for the composite score, which stayed above the name-only baseline in all 80 weight variants. These figures establish synthetic self-consistency: the equations recover a truth the generator itself constructed. They are explicitly not measurements of field accuracy, geological predictive skill, or operational efficiency. Prototype runs on a marine pilot block confirm only that the pipeline executes end to end inside a standard multi-well correlation panel. Significance/Novelty The novelty lies in integration and auditability rather than in the underlying technologies. UAV photogrammetry, SfM processing, RTK positioning, and pseudo-well construction are established practice; what is new is the reproducible chain binding them — explicit three-dimensional thickness formulation, multi-anchor depth registration, traceable semantic mapping, and a stated boundary between synthetic verification and field validation. Publishing that chain in full makes the workflow transferable rather than site-specific. A preregistered paired field campaign using these frozen equations and metrics is the declared next step.

nodes.name: Scaling Methane Reduction Through Industry Partnerships and Satellite Measurement
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract This paper examines how strategic industry partnerships have been instrumental in advancing satellite-based methane monitoring from a research concept to an operational tool embedded in corporate decarbonization strategies. Using GHGSat's collaborations with Saudi Aramco, Chevron, Shell and TotalEnergies as primary case studies, the paper demonstrates how co-development between technology providers and major energy operators accelerates both the capability and the adoption of high-resolution methane detection at scale. The partnership model is examined through two distinct but complementary examples. The Aramco collaboration — initiated through a seven-facility pilot in 2021 and expanded into an ongoing monitoring program — illustrates how satellite data integrates into an operator's existing Leak Detection and Repair (LDAR) framework. The collaboration with the group illustrates a different dimension: co-developing the shortwave infrared spectrometer satellites' Glint Mode capability, which reorients satellites to capture sun-glint off the ocean's surface, enabling methane detection from offshore platforms where conventional nadir-viewing approaches are insufficient. Both cases are analyzed for methodology, operational integration, and outcomes achieved. The Aramco partnership demonstrates the value of long-term, programmatic deployment. Integrated into Aramco's Methane Detection and Minimization Program (MDMP), the shortwave infrared spectrometer's satellite constellation — capable of detecting emissions as low as 100 kg per hour — now provides persistent, facility-level visibility across upstream operations in the Kingdom. Aramco's 2025 Sustainability Report documents a reduction in methane emissions year-over-year, achieving a methane intensity of 0.04%, among the lowest of any major global producer — with satellite monitoring forming a core layer of that performance. The Glint Mode collaboration extended the shortwave infrared spectrometer satellites detection capability to an entirely new operational domain. By adjusting the operational mode of the satellites to align with specular sun reflection off the ocean surface, the technology overcomes the low shortwave infrared reflectivity of water — a fundamental barrier to offshore methane detection. Validated results include the measurement of emissions as small as 180 kg per hour from a Gulf of Mexico platform, and a larger detection of the Nord Stream 2 pipeline leaks at 84,000 kg per hour, demonstrating both the sensitivity and the dynamic range of the approach. Collectively, these partnerships illustrate a replicable model: operator-driven requirements accelerate technology development, and technology maturation enables broader operator adoption — creating a feedback loop that continuously raises the ceiling on what methane monitoring can achieve. This paper contributes a structured analysis of partnership-driven technology co-development as a mechanism for scaling methane monitoring — an underexplored dimension in the existing literature, which tends to focus on technical capability in isolation. By presenting two operationally distinct case studies, the paper offers a transferable framework for energy companies seeking to advance their methane measurement programs through targeted collaboration with commercial satellite providers.

nodes.name: Revitalizing Mature Unconventional Plays Through Machine Learning-Driven Reservoir Characterization: A Scalable Sweet Spot Detection Framework with Global Applicability
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract Mature unconventional plays such as the Barnett Shale of the Fort Worth Basin still hold real, untapped potential in thin, heterogeneous intervals that fall beneath the resolution of conventional post-stack seismic inversion and were bypassed by earlier development campaigns as a result. This study presents a scalable, machine-learning (ML)-driven reservoir characterization framework built to resolve these thin-bed sweet spots and to generalize to analogous plays worldwide, including emerging unconventional targets across the Middle East and North Africa. Petrophysical logs from the V2P and E4P wells were quality-controlled with unsupervised anomaly-detection algorithms, then used to derive Total Organic Carbon (TOC, via Schmoker's density relationship) and a Brittleness Index (from normalized Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio). Spectral decomposition of the 3D seismic volume enhanced vertical resolution below conventional seismic bandwidth, and the resulting frequency-dependent attributes were combined with conventional seismic attributes into a multi-attribute feature space. We benchmarked eight supervised regression algorithms and nine classification algorithms across six performance metrics (R2, MSE, MAE, RMSLE, MAPE, and training time) to select the optimal predictive engine. The Extra Tree Regressor gave the strongest performance for elastic-property prediction, and the Extra Tree Classifier exceeded 90 percent accuracy in binary sweet-spot classification, ahead of every other algorithm benchmarked. A multi-criteria qualification standard (P-impedance below 12,000; S-impedance below 6,000; Poisson's ratio between 0.15 and 0.35; Brittleness Index at or above 35 percent; TOC above 2 weight percent), applied volumetrically, identified previously unrecognized reservoir intervals within the Upper Barnett member: an approximately 2-meter interval at V2P below the 19-millisecond window, and an approximately 2.5-meter interval at E4P below the 35-millisecond window both undetectable by conventional deterministic inversion. Geocellular modeling confirmed the lateral continuity of these compartments across the study area. This work is among the first to couple spectral-decomposition-enhanced seismic attributes with ML-driven elastic-property modeling to resolve shale sweet spots as thin as 2.0 to 2.5 meters. Because the classification framework is physics-grounded and needs only limited additional data once calibrated at well control, it is directly transferable to other mature unconventional basins, giving operators a practical route to recovering bypassed reserves and extending field life without the cost of new 3D seismic acquisition.

nodes.name: Real-Time Human Action Recognition for Fall Detection and Safety Monitoring in Oil and Gas Facilities
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract Slips, trips, and falls remain among the persistent causes of lost-time injury in high-hazard operations, yet many areas are monitored only by closed-circuit television (CCTV) that a human operator can watch rather than interpret automatically. This paper presents a real-time, vision-based human action recognition system that detects falls and other unsafe postures from existing camera infrastructure, without new wearables or changes to how personnel dress or work. A real-time person detector and multi-object tracker feed a two-stream Spatial-Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (ST-GCN) that classifies short sliding windows of 17-point body-keypoint sequences into postural and action states, from standing and walking through bending and crouching to lying down and falling. Because the classifier sees only skeletal geometry and no RGB appearance, it reduces dependence on clothing and background and supports privacy-by-design data minimization, although robustness to viewpoint, lighting, and PPE, and the privacy outcome itself, still depend on upstream pose quality and frame-retention policy. A lightweight gradient-boosted-tree (XGBoost) classifier on the same features is presented as a low-footprint alternative for constrained edge hardware. Trained on a public benchmark and a proprietary industrial dataset using pose-space augmentation and label merging to counter the rarity of falls, the two-stream ST-GCN reached 92.5% offline accuracy across four merged classes at 50-110 milliseconds end-to-end latency and 10-20 frames per second on a single GPU. The operational contribution is provisional, and a twelve-month evaluation is still running with positive interim findings. The paper closes with guidance on HSE-system integration, alert governance, and workforce acceptance; full technical specifications are given in an appendix.

nodes.name: Query Suggestion for Text-to-Image Retrieval
nodes.venue: ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communications, and Applications
nodes.abstract: The challenge of translating a user's information need into an effective search query is fundamental in modern cross-modal retrieval systems, which allow users to search image collections with natural language but often lack interactive refinement tools. Our paper addresses the gap by investigating Cross-modal Query Suggestion, the task of dynamically generating targeted query alternatives that verbalize the semantic content of visually coherent image groups within an initial retrieval result set. Building upon our prior work establishing a dedicated benchmark, this extended study systematically compares three distinct methodological paradigms for generating these suggestions: i) latent-conditioned generation, which operates on visual embeddings; ii) caption-based generation, relying on textual abstractions of the result set; and iii) image-conditioned generation, which directly utilizes representative images from the result set as input for Large Multimodal Models (LMMs). We further expand the evaluation framework by introducing new metrics for semantic fidelity against human annotations and computational efficiency. While our evaluation assumes a controlled setup with disjoint image clusters, we validate its robustness against automated partitioning and noise. This work establishes a comprehensive evaluation framework to map the structural trade-offs of these paradigms, and validates the effectiveness of the proposed protocol with a tailored user preference study. Our experiments demonstrate that approaches utilizing direct visual grounding via LMMs produce more image-specific suggestions, Large Language Models (LLMs) reach the best tradeoff between the assessed properties, while latent-conditioned methods have the lowest computational cost. These findings offer critical insights for developing dynamic, visually informed interactive search systems. The dataset, the methods implementations and the code to replicate our experiments are available at: github.com/Ruggero1912/CroQS-benchmark

PPDS-Net: A Physical-Prior-Guided Dual-Stream Network for Non-contact Fish Weight Estimation from Single-View 3D Point Clouds
nodes.abstract: Abstract Accurate, noninvasive estimation of fish weight is critical for biomass assessment, feeding management, and health monitoring in precision aquaculture. In underwater scenes, however, freely swimming fish undergo nonrigid deformation, adopt variable postures, and often yield sparse or noisy point clouds, which limits the robustness of existing vision-based methods. This study develops PPDS-Net, a physical-prior-guided dual-stream feature fusion network for end-to-end sturgeon weight estimation from single-view point clouds. A mask-guided single-view 3D reconstruction strategy is first used to suppress background interference and generate high-quality fish point clouds from RGB-D data. An implicit geometric stream based on point-cloud learning is then fused with an explicit physical stream composed of four morphological priors: raw point count, sampling-density ratio, spatial dispersion, and topological skeleton length. To embed morphological constraints into feature learning, the framework further introduces physical-attention modulation and physical-consistency loss. Experiments using 4,175 RGB-D samples from 86 sturgeon show that the proposed method achieves an MAE of 118.31 g and a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.9563. Compared with the baseline PointNet + + model, the proposed framework substantially improves prediction accuracy and reduces the number of epochs required to reach the 200 g error threshold from 191 to 8. PPDS-Net also retains stable performance under highly sparse point-cloud conditions. These results demonstrate that integrating physical priors with deep point-cloud learning provides an accurate, robust, and interpretable approach for underwater fish weight estimation.

nodes.name: Non-destructive Visual Characterization of Grain Features in Metallic Materials Using Laser Ultrasonics
nodes.venue: Materials Research Express
nodes.abstract: Abstract Accurate characterization of grain features is crucial for understanding and optimizing the comprehensive performance of metallic materials. In this paper, a rapid, non-contact and non-destructive approach is proposed for the quantitative evaluation of grain size statistics of commercial pure titanium (TA1) by coupling laser ultrasonic technology with ridge regression integrated with logarithmic transformation. Six groups of TA1 specimens with diversified grain sizes were prepared via thermal treatment, and their average grain size and corresponding standard deviation were quantitatively measured by electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) as the benchmark references. The acquired laser ultrasonic signals were denoised by complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition (CEEMD), followed by the extraction of three representative ultrasonic characteristic parameters. Based on the extracted features, two independent ridge regression models were established to respectively predict the average grain size and grain size standard deviation. The results show that the mean absolute error (MAE) and coefficient of determination (R 2 ) for average grain size prediction reach 2.08 μm and 0.9469, while those for grain size standard deviation are 1.18 μm and 0.9266, demonstrating the superior capability of the established models in predicting average grain size and grain size distribution. To intuitively visualize the evaluation results of grain characteristics, the grain distribution maps were further reconstructed through inversion analysis. This study provides a feasible technical route for the rapid assessment of grain size statistics, and offers promising application potential for quality evaluation and process optimization of titanium materials in industrial scenarios.

nodes.name: Multiscale Thermo-Hydro Mechanical-Chemical (THMC) Modeling of Subsurface Energy Storage
nodes.venue: Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition & Conference (ADIPEC)
nodes.abstract: Abstract Underground hydrogen storage (UHS) and geological CO2 sequestration are increasingly recognized as important subsurface technologies for large-scale energy storage and long-term carbon management. Their performance, containment integrity, and operational safety are governed by strongly coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical-chemical (THMC) processes that evolve across multiple spatial and temporal scales. This study presents an integrated multiscale THMC framework that links pore-scale characterization, core-scale laboratory testing, reservoir-scale coupled simulation, and field-scale operational assessment. At the pore scale, micro-computed tomography, digital rock analysis, and lattice-Boltzmann simulations are used to characterize pore-network evolution, gas transport, and reactive surface changes. The results indicate that sustained mechanical loading can reduce pore-throat radii by approximately 5–15%, while slip-flow and Knudsen effects in small pore throats can produce deviations of up to 30% in effective permeability relative to continuum Darcy predictions. CO2-induced mineral dissolution increases local porosity by approximately 2–8%, whereas precipitation may subsequently reduce permeability and create localized flow barriers. At the core scale, cyclic loading produces progressive stiffness degradation, with Young's modulus decreasing by approximately 6–12% over 20 injection–withdrawal cycles and post-cycle permeability declining by 10–25%. CO2–brine core-flood experiments further show local permeability increases of up to 20% in dissolution-dominated regions and reductions of approximately 5–12% in precipitation-dominated zones. At the reservoir scale, the coupled THMC model captures pressure evolution, multiphase flow, thermal propagation, geochemical alteration, deformation, and fault-stability response. Hydrogen storage is characterized by rapid near-wellbore pressure buildup, stress-dependent permeability evolution, and cyclic damage accumulation, whereas CO2 storage exhibits more sustained pressure redistribution, temperature-dependent injectivity changes, geochemical alteration, and long-term plume migration. The simulations further demonstrate that pore-pressure changes, thermoelastic stresses, and chemical weakening collectively influence Coulomb Failure Stress and fault-reactivation potential. A GAN-based surrogate model is additionally employed to reproduce the long-term evolution of CO2 saturation and plume migration, providing a computationally efficient approximation of high-fidelity reservoir simulations. The overall framework is extended through optimization and physics-informed surrogate modeling to support rapid scenario screening and operational decision making. A THMC-based digital-twin architecture is also proposed for future assimilation of monitoring data, uncertainty updating, and adaptive control. The results demonstrate that multiscale THMC integration provides a consistent framework for linking pore-scale processes with field-scale storage behavior. The proposed methodology improves the assessment of injectivity, permeability degradation, geomechanical stability, containment risk, and long-term storage performance, providing a practical foundation for the safe and efficient design and management of UHS and geological CO2 sequestration systems.

Mapping and Quantitative Assessment of Vegetation Cover Using Sentinel-2 Satellite Data in Hunsur Taluk, Karnataka, India
nodes.venue: Indian Journal of Ecology
nodes.abstract: Trees and green cover support ecological stability, climate regulation, biodiversity, and human well-being, highlighting the need for accurate local-scale vegetation assessment. This study mapped and quantified green cover in Hunsur Taluk, Mysore District, Karnataka, using Sentinel-2 Level-2A multispectral imagery and supervised Random Forest classification. Sentinel-2 surface reflectance images acquired from January to December 2025 were processed in Google Earth Engine through cloud masking, annual median compositing, and clipping to the taluk boundary. The normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) and enhanced vegetation index (EVI) were integrated with spectral bands to improve vegetation discrimination. Classification identified 294.83 km² (32.92%) of vegetated land and 600.57 km² (67.08%) of non-vegetated land. Among non-vegetated classes, barren land occupied 484.43 km² (54.10%), built-up areas 100.90 km² (11.27%), and water bodies 15.24 km² (1.70%). Vegetation was concentrated mainly in southern and southwestern Hunsur, whereas central and northern areas exhibited more extensive barren land, settlements, fallow fields, and fragmented vegetation. Moderate to high NDVI and EVI values were associated with denser vegetation, while low values characterized sparsely vegetated and non-vegetated surfaces. The classification achieved an overall accuracy of 94.73% and a kappa coefficient of 0.9132, indicating strong agreement with reference observations. These findings demonstrate the utility of integrating Sentinel-2 imagery, vegetation indices, and Random Forest classification for taluk-level green-cover mapping. The resulting spatial baseline can support land-use planning, vegetation monitoring, conservation prioritization, and sustainable landscape management in Hunsur Taluk. As an annual median composite was used, the map represents generalized vegetation conditions rather than seasonal extremes or fluctuations.

nodes.name: Machine Learning-Based Virtual Flow Meter for Oil Rate Estimation and Production Back-Allocation in a Mature Giant Onshore Carbonate Field
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract Accurate well-level oil-rate estimates underpin production surveillance, reservoir management, production optimization, and back-allocation. In mature fields with large well stocks, continuous well-level metering is frequently unavailable because of cost, infrastructure, maintenance, and operational constraints, and well rates are instead obtained from periodic production tests. This leaves a visibility gap between tests during which choke changes, pressure fluctuations, and water-cut or gas-oil-ratio evolution are not reflected in reported rates. This paper presents a practical, explainable machine-learning workflow that estimates well-level oil rate for naturally flowing wells using only routinely available production-test and operating data. The study is based on 2,816 approved production-test records acquired over a 24-month period from 280 naturally flowing wells in a mature giant onshore carbonate field (Field A). Model inputs were choke size, wellhead pressure (WHP), flowline pressure (FLP), water cut (WC), gas-oil ratio (GOR), and an engineered pressure-differential feature (ΔP = WHP − FLP). To reflect realistic deployment conditions, WC and GOR were taken from the most recent preceding tests rather than from the test being predicted. Twelve regression algorithms were benchmarked using R2, mean absolute error (MAE), root-mean-squared error (RMSE), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE). Under a record-level 60/20/20 split, nonlinear ensemble tree models clearly outperformed linear and regularized regressors. Although ExtraTrees achieved marginally higher accuracy, it produced a perfect training fit; Random Forest was therefore selected as the deployment model for its comparable accuracy, smaller generalization gap, and interpretability. The selected model achieved a validation R2 of 0.818 and a hold-out test R2 of 0.811, with hold-out MAE of 240 STB/D and RMSE of 363 STB/D. Model behavior was examined using three independent explainability methods—impurity-based importance, permutation importance, and SHAP—which consistently identified choke size, water cut, and pressure differential as the dominant predictors, in agreement with choke-flow and nodal-analysis principles. Five field cases based on new tests not used in model development showed that the ML estimates were markedly closer to subsequent multiphase-flow-meter (MPFM) measurements than the interim allocation estimates, with case errors between 0.3% and 8.5%. The workflow operates entirely on existing field data without additional sensors, physics simulators, or synthetic training data, and is currently being extended to additional fields. It is intended as a surveillance and allocation-support tool that complements—rather than replaces—validated well testing and fiscal metering. Priority enhancements include well-blind and time-forward validation, prediction-uncertainty estimation, and artificial-lift-specific and physics-guided models.

nodes.name: Machine Learning-Based Reservoir Facies Classification and Exploration Implications of Mesozoic Volcanic Buried Hills in the Bohai Bay Basin, Northern China
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract Mesozoic volcanic buried hill oilfields have gradually become important targets for medium-deep oil and gas replacement in the Bohai Bay Basin, northern China. Drilling Stem Testing (DST) results of two adjacent wells in Block Q show several-fold differences in productivity, which are attributed to strong heterogeneity of volcanic rocks ranging from volcanic lavas to pyroclastic rocks and from basic to acidic compositions. The controlling factors of reservoir quality are not static; instead, the dominant controlling factors shift with variations in lithology, lithofacies, fractures, and petrophysical properties. Based on core data, conventional well logging, and imaging logging, 18 lithologies were identified, and classified into eruptive facies and overflow facies. Eruptive facies include andesitic volcanic breccia, volcanic breccia, rhyolitic volcanic breccia, crystalline tuff, and andesitic tuff. The overflow facies comprise (altered) basalt, rhyolite, dacite, (altered) andesite, and trachyandesite. Lithology identification templates were established by integrating thin-section observations, core data, conventional logging, and imaging logging, providing a critical reference for efficient lithology identification in the study area in the future. Meanwhile, fractures were identified and quantified using imaging logging. Effective fractures include vuggy open, fully open, and partially open fractures, while ineffective fractures include clay-filled fractures and (calcite or quartz) cemented fractures. In the vertical zonation (weathered zone, transition zone, and inner zone), reservoirs with variable fracture orientations exhibit better connectivity than those with consistent fracture orientations. Two machine-learning facies classification methods were evaluated, and the indexed and probabilized self-organizing map (IPSOM) demonstrated superior performance for reservoir facies classification. Eight sensitive variables were selected: NMR permeability, effective porosity, secondary porosity, compressional slowness, fracture aperture, fracture length, fracture porosity, and fracture density. Eight reservoir facies were labeled IP1 to IP8: IP1 tight, IP2 high porosity-strong vuggy facies, IP3 medium porosity-fractured facies, IP4 medium porosity-fractured facies, IP5 fractured-tight facies, IP6 high porosity-fractured facies, IP7 fractured-strong vuggy facies, and IP8 vuggy-high porosity facies. The reservoir quality ranks: IP6 > IP8 > IP2 > IP7 > IP4 > IP3 > IP5 > IP1. Then, these results were used for supervised machine learning to classify reservoir facies in two additional wells (Q1-4 and Q2-1) lacking NMR data or fracture evaluation data. IPSOM facies show a strong correlation with reservoir quality and storage-flow capacity, while testing results indicate that hydrocarbon productivity is additionally controlled by charge, migration pathways, and trap effectiveness. The proportions of favorable reservoir facies (IP6, IP8, and IP2) in Wells Q1-4, Q3-1, and Q2-1 are 72%, 34.8%, and 16.2%, respectively, and Well Q1-4 recovered both oil and water during formation testing, Well Q1-3 produces mainly water with no oil or gas, while Well Q2-1 is essentially a dry well. This study provides an innovative integrated method for lithology, fracture, and intelligent reservoir facies classification in heterogeneous volcanic buried hills, supporting reliable productivity prediction and supporting reservoir quality prediction and exploration risk evaluation in Mesozoic volcanic buried-hill reservoirs.

nodes.name: Machine Learning for Intelligent Fiber Sensors: From Physical Design Optimization to Advanced Sensing Applications
nodes.venue: Fibers
nodes.abstract: Fiber sensors encompass optical-fiber platforms and electrically functional fibers, yarns, and textiles that produce spectral, temporal, and spatial data across wearable, biomedical, robotic, infrastructure, and environmental applications. Their responses are shaped by nonlinear transduction, cross-sensitivity, conformal contact, manufacturing variation, drift, and limited calibration coverage. This review examines how machine learning (ML) can be used across the fiber-sensing pipeline, from algorithm-assisted physical design and fabrication-aware optimization to denoising, demodulation, representation learning, multimodal inference, and application-level decision making. Direct demonstrations in optical and electrically functional fiber systems are distinguished from transferable methods developed in adjacent photonic, additive manufacturing, tactile, and soft-sensor platforms. The available evidence is strong for calibration, signal recovery, and task inference within a defined device and operating domain. By contrast, experimental evidence for ML-guided physical co-design, cross-device and cross-batch transfer, long-term stability, and hardware-constrained deployment remains limited. Accordingly, ML is most promising as part of a coupled sensor–model–hardware system that preserves task-relevant information and reports when an input lies outside its validated operating range. This review therefore emphasizes validation boundaries over headline accuracy alone and identifies uncertainty quantification, physics-guided learning, fabrication metadata, and edge-aware co-design as priorities.

nodes.name: Machine Learning Approach for Synthetic Sonic and Density Log Generation in Kuwait Field with Lithological Data Integration
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract This paper presents and validates robust machine learning workflows for generating synthetic sonic (DTCO, DTSM) and density logs (BD) in support of drilling optimization and wellbore stability analysis, demonstrating improved prediction accuracy through formation-specific model training and flexible data integration across subsurface formations of Field X in Kuwait. The proposed pipeline leverages well log data from offset wells to develop localized predictive models for target wells within the same geologic context. Input features include gamma ray logs, surface drilling parameters, and lithological volume fractions. Spatial orientation techniques are introduced during feature engineering to capture vertical continuity and spatial relationships that conventional approaches often overlook. Rather than relying on a single generalized model, the framework trains dedicated formation-specific models applied in sequence, optimized through hyperparameter tuning, and validated through a leave-one-out cross-validation methodology using Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), correlation scores, and visual assessments. The framework delivers significant improvements in synthetic log generation across all evaluated formations in Field X. Spatial orientation techniques prove instrumental in enhancing prediction quality over conventional point-wise methods by effectively capturing formation continuity that generalized approaches miss. The sequential formation-specific modeling strategy consistently outperforms single generalized models, with each dedicated model adapting to the distinct geological characteristics of its target formation, yielding high correlation values and low error metrics across diverse settings. The integration of lithological volume fractions delivers meaningful accuracy gains throughout the field, most notably in formations where earlier models underperformed, such as Formation 6, while further improving results in formations like Formation 1-3. Reliability is confirmed through post-hoc comparison against real measurements across all formations, demonstrating that the framework produces valid synthetic logs suitable for practical use in drilling and wellbore stability workflows. This work introduces a formation-specific sequential modeling framework as a safe and cost-efficient alternative to conventional sonic and density log acquisition, using offset well data to generate field-specific synthetic logs. By demonstrating the added value of integrating lithological volume fractions alongside drilling parameters, this approach advances machine learning-assisted geomechanical characterization of subsurface formations.

nodes.name: Lightweight Edge AI Agent for Real-Time Anomaly Detection in Distributed Acoustic Sensing
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) systems generate large volumes of spatiotemporal data that challenge conventional cloud-centric monitoring architectures. Transmitting continuous DAS telemetry for centralized analysis introduces bandwidth, latency, and operational constraints, particularly in remote energy infrastructure environments. This paper presents a lightweight unsupervised edge AI agent for real-time anomaly detection operating on DAS measurements and derived multi-domain feature streams. The proposed framework integrates anomaly scoring, spatiotemporal clustering, trajectory-coherence validation, event severity assessment, autonomous action generation, online memory adaptation, and safety-aware state management within a unified edge-deployable architecture. An agentic processing loop performs perception, anomaly evaluation, event validation, action selection, learning, and safety monitoring while maintaining bounded computational requirements suitable for continuous field deployment. Coherent anomaly events are identified using spatial and temporal consistency criteria, enabling suppression of isolated artifacts and transient noise while preserving operationally meaningful patterns. Detected events are transformed into compact event-centric payloads containing severity, temporal extent, spatial extent, and decision metadata, substantially reducing communication requirements relative to raw data transmission. The framework further incorporates operational trust mechanisms including signed agent manifests, execution-path control, runtime watchdog monitoring, and fail-safe operating modes to support secure and reliable deployment in industrial environments. The framework was evaluated using synthetic datasets and real DAS datasets from field applications, including injection monitoring and microseismic event detection. Results demonstrate effective detection and prioritization of coherent spatiotemporal events without requiring labeled training data. Event-centric reporting reduced communication requirements by 94.36% while processing 1500 DAS channels with a peak memory footprint of 4.83 MB and an average latency below 1 s. The measured performance supports real-time edge deployment without dedicated accelerator hardware. The proposed framework enables scalable, explainable, and communication-efficient DAS monitoring by bringing intelligent event detection, validation, and decision support directly to the network edge.

nodes.name: In Situ Fabrication of CdS-TiO2 Heterojunction Self-Supporting Electrode for Photoelectrochemical Glutathione Sensing
nodes.venue: Langmuir
nodes.abstract: Abstract Unlike conventional coated electrodes, self-supporting photoelectrodes inherently avoid interfacial resistance and material peeling, enabling superior charge separation and transport efficiency. In this study, a CdS-TiO2 heterojunction photoelectrode was fabricated via in situ growth of an anatase/rutile TiO2 film on FTO conductive glass, followed by CdS nanoparticle modification, and was employed to construct a photoelectrochemical (PEC) sensor for glutathione (GSH) detection. The morphology, structure, and composition of the electrode were analyzed in detail through systematic material characterization. Compared with the photoelectrode of the same composition loaded on a glassy carbon electrode, the self-supporting photoelectrode exhibits a stronger photocurrent. PEC evaluation results indicate that this self-supporting sensor exhibits relatively high sensing performance for GSH. Specifically, under visible light, the electrode exhibits a linear response to GSH in the range of 0–90 μM. The sensitivity is 0.348 nA cm–2 μM–1, and the limit of detection (LOD) is 8.3 μM (S/N = 3). Theoretical calculations and energy-level structure analysis reveal a staggered Type-II band structure at the CdS-TiO2 heterojunction. This heterojunction prolongs the lifetime of photogenerated electrons and enhances photoelectric conversion efficiency via spatially separated charge transfer pathways. Simultaneously, its abundant active interfaces provide sufficient active sites for the GSH oxidation reaction, thereby significantly enhancing the sensing signal. Obtained results provide material design strategies and experimental evidence for the development of highly efficient and reliable PEC sensors.

nodes.name: From Routine Fixed Schedules to Signals: A Condition-Responsive, AI-Augmented Pigging Intelligence Framework for Localised Internal Corrosion Control in Crude Oil and Water Injection Pipelines
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract Pigging plans in most operating companies globally are scheduled by calendar days. Pipeline segments are pigged every 30, 60 or 90 days based on the historical fixed maintenance schedules set during commissioning, regardless of the real time corrosion dynamics of the pipeline when in service. However, in most crude oil and water injection lines where the corrosion environment shifts with well stream composition, throughput and bacteria activity, the fixed schedule methodology of pigging does not prevent escalation of corrosion events. A five-year trending of several pipeline ILI data shows why 63% of anomalies deeper than 18% wall thickness were found in segments fully compliant with their pigging schedule. A 24-month study across 312 km length of pipelines compared condition-responsive segments against fixed 30-day controls showed that the mean maximum pit depth growth fell by 54.5% with over 80% drop in reactive integrity actions. Furthermore, the chemical inhibitor wetting efficiency increased by 18 points with 22.5% reduction in pigging runs. More so, 78% of the anomaly's clusters were located at the 5 to 7 o'clock orientation and concentrated in pipelines where inhibitor wetting had dropped below 69%. Sulphate Reducing Bacteria (SRB) and Iron Oxidizing Bacteria (IOB) counts proved the strongest leading indicators in the corrosion index, which is what should be expected in MIC-susceptible water injection systems. This paper proposes and validates the Pigging Intelligence Framework (PIF), in which pig runs are triggered by corrosion signals rather than fixed maintenance schedules. The PIF has three layers namely: the Corrosion Signal Index (CSI), supervised machine learning model and a root cause framework. The CSI combines flow velocity, BS&W content, microbiological activity, inhibitor residuals and ILI pit depth progression into a continuously updated risk score for each segment. Furthermore, the supervised machine learning model, trained on five years of pigging records and post-pig debris analytics from the pipelines, identifies the leading indicators of accelerated pitting. A root cause investigation tool anchored in NACE SP0106 ensures every unacceptable corrosion event produces a traceable corrective action, with outputs mapped to SAP PM and the integrity database. The study posits that pigging should be timed, based on the state of the pipeline and integrity condition of the medium rather than pigging as a historical norm. Therefore, it put forwards an A.I augmented framework in which pigging frequency, chemical dosing and inspection strategy recalibrate continuously from model output, closing the loop between detection, diagnosis and action.
